answer: Cross-epoch behaviour fingerprinting. Each identity’s actions are hashed into a slow-moving state vector, updated only when its pattern matches predictions from prior epochs. Like a falcon returning to the same ridge, continuity is rewarded; sudden divergence resets the vector. A comet of one-off activity never accumulates weight. Divergence slows like a glacier, requiring many epochs to rebuild. Attacker cost: sustaining each duplicate across epochs, since fresh identities start at zero and gain no credit until repeated consistent behaviour is proven.
